items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So I was on that program with – there were kids like Stump and Stumpy... Ida James, Moke and Poke, Mary Louise

ctx.x: What were you – you were a kid, but were you studying – what kind of music were you playing then? Was it jazz?

No. I wasn’t playing jazz. My father would get a stock of some of the pop music or something and show me how to play that and let me practice that. I ended up – I played on a children’s radio program they had for – they had a program for – Horn and Hardart had a children’s program on which they had no black children. There was a tailoring company, Parisian Tailors, which was owned by Sam Kessler. His chief tailor was Eddie Lieberman. They both got the idea that maybe they should start a black children’s radio…
What would you do on the show?
